Documentation

What NeuraWall detects without decrypting.

NeuraWall never decrypts traffic and never stores payloads. It works from flow metadata, so what it can find depends on what the sensor can see.

Visible in encrypted traffic

SignalUsed byWhat it can find
Flow shape: bytes in and out, packet counts, durations, timingTier 1 anomaly engine (Isolation Forest, EWMA baselines)A host that suddenly behaves differently, scans, floods
Inter-arrival timing of one flowBeacon detectorRegular call-backs to a server (C2 beaconing)
Volume and directionExfiltration detectorVery large outbound transfers (20 MB and up)
TLS handshake: SNI, TLS version, JA3 / JA4, ALPNTLS mismatch detectorA client claiming to be a browser with a non-browser fingerprint
DNS query namesDNS detectorDGA-looking names and DNS tunnelling

Needs the request visible

Needs the request visible (plain HTTP, or a sensor behind your TLS terminator)Used by
HTTP path and queryInjection detector: SQL, command and template injection, path traversal, XSS

The honest limit

On a public HTTPS service the injection detector sees nothing unless the sensor sits behind the TLS terminator, or you already run sensor-side decryption. Tier 1 and the signals in the first table work either way.

The detectors are heuristics with known gaps, and we publish them: see the Tier 2 evasion report. A detector can only raise an alert; a person approves any rule that blocks.
